title: The Turning Night
pitch: One compact wood bowl of about 40 screens, played three times as the night turns. At Dusk her kind sleeps in sheets on every trunk, the wood is dark and quiet, and one warm light moves through it: the firefly, stringing unlit lamps. At Lampfall (minute 4) the firefly kindles the whole wood in one sweep while she watches from a snag. The waking swarm rises straight into the lights and breaks into three great knots, and the same rooms turn into a dense, fast fling playground full of the predators the light pulled in. Then comes Silk. Every cloud she frees flies for the Moongate, the one gap in the canopy where the moon shows, and lands in a web that grows with each cloud. When the third lands, the wood goes dark again and is spun over: strands across the old roads, larders to cut open, danglers that hunt by touch. The night gates the level more than abilities do. Dusk shows the places she can't reach, Lampfall hangs the roads to them, and Silk closes the old ways and opens the climb. It's fun because every room is new three times, quiet and intense are the same place an hour apart, the world answers what she does, and you can read the time from the web across the moon.
throughline: Wing wants her swarm out of the lit wood and through the Moongate to the moon, because tonight is the night they fly and they are dying at the lights.

regions.name: The Cocoon Bough
regions.note: Dusk only on the critical path. Split cocoons, Tatter on the branch, the swarm asleep on every trunk across the bowl. Moss tufts to cut, sleepers that burst and resettle when she runs through them, and far off the firefly's warm point moving across the canopy.

regions.name: The Sleeping Wall
regions.note: A tall bark cliff down the west slope. DUSK: sheets of sleeping moths. She brushes them, they shiver off and resettle. Juvenile beetles eat the fallen, and the firefly's first lit glow-cap hangs over the top gap (the first fling, 1:10). LIT: knot C, the Wick Curtain, dozens of wicks hung where the moths slept and a knot spinning through them. Pogo down it flame by flame, or fling up it from the floor, with danglers where she has to stop. SILK: strands across the face, a larder bundle.

regions.name: The Drying Glade
regions.note: A moonlit shelf tucked into the wall's foot: GLIDE (her wings dry). The way out is back up a short ledge onto the snag.

regions.name: The Lookout Snag
regions.note: A dead limb jutting over the bowl. The vista: the Roost Gum in the middle, the Moongate east with the moon in it. Full dark falls, the swarm rises off every tree, and then the Lampfall. She keeps control throughout: glide off early and you watch it from the air.

regions.name: The Fernfall
regions.note: The bowl's west floor and the tall air over it that the Lampfall glide drops through; met first lit. Wicks in a line across fern hummocks, a beetle in each light pool, stragglers to free, ferns to hack. SILK: spiderling nests in the hummocks, and strands between the stems that tell the danglers where she is.

regions.name: The Roost Gum
regions.note: The hub: a giant hollow gum, from its floor up to its first limbs. Moon patch, moth-stone, Tatter. It shows the night: at DUSK its bark is furred with sleepers; LIT, bare bark with lamps strung up its limbs (the fling ladder to the boughs), and all three knots in view from the floor (chandelier overhead, curtain to the west, the Drowned Lantern glowing up through the roots); in SILK, strands hang from its limbs and the moon falls down its hollow.

regions.name: The High Boughs
regions.note: The canopy road, shut at dusk (you can see bare hooks from the snag) and opened by Lampfall. Knot B, the Hawker Chandelier: five lanterns on one limb, a knot of ~60 moths, two hawkers diving through the orbit. One clean chain through all five frees it in a single burst, and a miss lets the embers relight. Leaves to hack, a beetle on the broad limb, and the long glide west back to the wall top.

regions.name: The Firefly's Wake
regions.note: Optional and hard: the line of lamps the firefly lit in one fast stroke during the Lampfall, still burning as a dotted line across the canopy. A precise fling gauntlet over thorn-crowned limbs that follows its exact flight, with the embers retry and a checkpoint each screen. Any lamps left lit into Silk are webbed and harder.

regions.name: The Firefly's Cache
regions.note: Where the stroke ended: its stash of unlit glow-caps strung but never hung, a ring of lights in its flash pattern (firefly sign), a moon-drop (+1 health). A fling playground with no thorns.

regions.name: The Root Cellar
regions.note: Under the Roost. Knot A, the Drowned Lantern: a big lantern the firefly dropped down the hollow sits in a root pool, the knot spins low over the water, and the old burrback has grown huge on the moths that fall. Three phases (slam, roll, rams she baits into the taproot). The last ram breaks the root plug and the moon falls down the hollow trunk: CLAWS. Carrier ants on trails, root bark to break, a dark way round the pool.

regions.name: The Hollow of Wings
regions.note: Behind a bark wall at the cellar's west end: the floor under the Sleeping Wall's roots, where years of moths that died at lights came to rest. The first firefly sign (its rhythm, played once), the long-breath hollow (a longer fling aim), the drowned-roots stub.

regions.name: The Beetle Wallow
regions.note: The east floor: fallen hollow logs over black mud. LIT: a wick field, beetles, a dangler over a log's mouth, and the Loom's foot in view, a lock she can't climb. SILK: the weaver's larder. Bundles of re-caught moths hang from the logs to be cut free (each one a small cloud), spiderlings boil out of the logs, and strands lie across the floor.

regions.name: The Loom
regions.note: Two giant trunks with a tall shaft of sky between them, and the web's guy lines anchored to them. Tatter sits at the foot looking up. The climb needs claws: kick between the trunks, cut strands or ride the guy lines, while danglers drop where you touch silk and the weaver's shadow crosses overhead. With claws before the third knot you can climb early and watch the half-spun web being built.

regions.name: The Moongate
regions.note: The one gap in the canopy rim, where the moon shows and the migration has always left. The firefly hung its Crown here, its brightest lamp, and the weaver spun its web round it because that is where moths funnel. The boss arena. After it, the moon falls through the gate: GUST.

regions.name: The Valley Road
regions.note: East over the rim: the valley's lamps below, the freed swarm streaming toward the moon, the firefly's light fleeing ahead. The area's exit.

landmarks.name: The Sleeping Wall / the Wick Curtain
The Drowned Lantern's glow through the roots

abilities.name: Gust (a wingbeat that snuffs at range, tears silk)

secrets.name: The Sleepers' Ring: long-breath hollow behind the wall
secrets.tell: At dusk the sleeping moths pack in a ring round one bare patch of bark, and a thread of cool mist leaks from it (moths roost by cool hollows). Cut through the sleepers, then the bark. Later the patch is only bare, which is a much weaker tell.

secrets.name: The shadow with no caster: a moon-drop above the hub
secrets.tell: Only while the Roost's limb lamps burn: their light throws the shadow of a ledge onto the inner trunk, though no ledge is visible. It is behind a leaf cover. Snuff those lamps and the shadow is gone.

secrets.name: The Firefly's Wake to its Cache
secrets.tell: If you watched the Lampfall instead of gliding off, you saw the firefly light one line of lamps in a single fast stroke east of the boughs and vanish upward. The line still burns, dotted across the canopy.

secrets.name: The Hollow of Wings
secrets.tell: In the cellar's still air, moth wings drift sideways out of a bark wall.

secrets.name: The big larder: a cloud and a moon-drop
secrets.tell: Silk only: one bundle high in the Wallow's roof twitches and is twice the size of the rest. Its line runs up to a limb you can reach from the Loom's first kick.

boss.name: The Weaver at the Moongate
boss.idea: Gentle, about 2 minutes, a direct descendant of the lab Weaver. It tests the fling, reading a thread, the claws and the pogo. The web hangs across the Moongate round the firefly's Crown, full of the moths she freed; the firefly itself is caught near the hub of the web, flashing fast. P1, the web: five lanterns anchor its rim. Fling from anchor to anchor and each snuff drops a section. Touching silk slows her (no grab, she keeps control), and the weaver runs to the spot she touched. P2, the drop: the web sags, and the weaver drops on silk from the canopy where its thread shows first, as the danglers taught. She kicks up the gate's two trunks to stay above it and cuts it while it hangs. P3, the limb: the web falls and the trapped moths pour out round her, the area's biggest release. The weaver lunges along the gate's limb, she pogoes its abdomen, then puts the Crown out flame by flame. Last, the strand holding the firefly snaps. Freed, it darts to the Crown, relights it behind her, and flees east (the Kuro beat: she saved it, and it undid her work). The moon falls through the gate and she gets Gust, whose first wingbeat puts the relit Crown out from across the gap. The stars come out over the whole bowl.

minuteByMinute: 0–1: Dusk. Black, then cool moonlight. She breaks the cocoon in 8 s. Every trunk across the bowl is furred with sleeping moths, and Tatter sits torn-winged on the branch. Running through the sleepers bursts them and they resettle. One warm point crosses the far canopy.

1–2: At the wall's top the warm point is close. The firefly hangs a glow-cap over the gap, lights it, pulses twice and darts off. It is the only warm light in the world. One straggler circles it. The first fling: time slows, aim, launch, and the straggler bursts free.
2–3: Down the Sleeping Wall through sheets of her kind. Juvenile beetles are eating the ones that fell (two cuts each). The Sleepers' Ring and its cool mist are there for the curious.

3–4: The Drying Glade: moonlight, her wings dry, glide. Back up onto the dead snag: the whole bowl, the Roost Gum, the moon in the Moongate. Full dark: the swarm lifts off every tree in one river toward the moon.

4–5: LAMPFALL. The firefly flies one circuit and the wood kindles behind it in a wave, hundreds of lamps. The river turns into the lights and breaks into three great knots. Title over the moon. She can glide off at any moment and is never held. The glide down into the lit wood passes a wick: the first mid-air fling.

5–7: The Fernfall, lit and the densest screen so far. Wicks in a line, a beetle in each light pool, stragglers, ferns to hack, a fling chain over the hummocks. The rooms she walked in the dark are now full of light and hunters.

7–8: The Roost Gum, the hub. Patch, moth-stone, Tatter, the only moth not caught (its torn wing saved it). From the floor all three knots are in view: the chandelier overhead, the curtain to the west, the glow under the floor. She picks; the ghost run goes up.

8–10: Up the lamps on the Roost's limbs to the boughs. The Hawker Chandelier: five lanterns, two hawkers through the orbit, one clean chain and the knot bursts free. Its cloud streams east toward the moon and stops dead in a few silver lines across the Moongate. The firefly flashes alarm from the Crown.

10–12: West along the boughs and a long glide to the wall's top. Knot C is the Wick Curtain, hung exactly where the moths slept two hours ago. Pogo down it flame by flame with danglers where she has to stop. The curtain goes dark behind her, and from the hub you can watch it go out.
12–13: Back across the Fernfall. Most of its lamps are already out, so it's dark and quick now. The web over the moon has spokes. Into the Roost and down through its floor.

13–15: The Root Cellar. The Drowned Lantern in its pool and the old burrback, fat on fallen moths: slam, roll, rams baited into the taproot. The last ram breaks the plug and the moon pours down the hollow trunk: claws. Knot A's cloud rises up the trunk, east, and into the web. The web is whole. SILK falls.

15–17: Kick up the hollow trunk (the shortcut). The Roost is dark again and silk hangs from every limb. Any lamp she left burning is webbed now. East into the Wallow: larders of re-caught moths to cut open, spiderlings boiling out of logs, strands on the floor that wake the danglers. Slow, tense, and dark.

17–19: The Loom. Tatter at its foot, looking up at a climb it can't make. She kicks up between the two trunks, cutting strands or riding the guy lines, while the weaver's shadow crosses the moon above.

19–22: The Weaver at the Moongate: snuff the anchors, survive the drops, pogo it on the limb, and put out the Crown. The web falls and every caught moth pours through the gate. The firefly, freed from the strand, relights the Crown behind her and flees east.

22–24: The moon falls through the gate: Gust. Its first wingbeat puts out the relit Crown across the gap. The stars come out over the whole bowl. The fallen web hangs to the floor, Tatter climbs it, and they go east to the valley's lights.
